analysis_steps.goal: Extract spatially-resolved stellar kinematics (V_rms map) from VLT/MUSE data

method.value: Remove telluric lines with ZAP, align astrometry to HST by 0.18'' with ASTROALIGN, exclude spaxels contaminated by strong lensed source emission, select spaxels with SNR > 2.0 in 5000-7000 A rest-frame, Voronoi-bin with VorBin to SNR >= 10, fit V and sigma_V with pPXF using Indo-US stellar templates, and compute V_rms = sqrt(V^2 + sigma_V^2).

evidence.quote: We use the Zurich Atmosphere Purge code (cite: ZAP) to remove telluric lines which may have been left in the previous reduction step.
we sum nearby spectra using the adaptive spatial two-dimensional binning scheme from `VorBin` package (cite: Vorbin_2003) to increase the SNR in each resulting Voronoi bin at a minimum of 10.
After fitting all the Voronoi bins, we construct the $V_\text{rms} = \sqrt{V^2 + \sigma_V^2}$ map, which is the root-mean-square velocity for each Voronoi bin.

analysis_steps.goal: Prepare ALMA Band 7 continuum image and error map for image-plane lens modelling

method.value: Bin the ALMA Band 7 continuum image from 0.005'' to 0.01'' pixels, rotate by PA = 11.9 deg, and build an error map from the background rms measured in CASA plus 10% of each pixel value added in quadrature.

evidence.quote: We use the image of continuum band 7, which includes the $\sim 250\mu$m rest-frame emission, for the lens modelling. The image was also binned from a pixel scale of $0.005\ensuremath{''}$ to a pixel scale of $0.01\ensuremath{''}$, to increase the modelling efficiency and reduce the covariance between the pixels (cite: Dye2015).

Moreover, the error map was estimated by the rms background value, measured using `CASA` in a region where no emission is seen, with the addition of $10$% of the value of each pixel summed in quadrature to account for possible calibration errors.

assumptions.value: Image-plane pixel covariance errors are small due to dense uv-plane coverage; lens galaxy light contamination is negligible in Band 7.

evidence.quote: Due to the wavelength observed by ALMA, the lens light is not visible, and only the deflected source is captured, making this dataset very suitable for lens modelling since the contamination due to the lens galaxy light is negligible.
However, due to the high coverage of the $uv-$plane in these ALMA data, the error associated with the image plane is significantly reduced.

analysis_steps.goal: Perform 5-phase joint Bayesian modelling of ALMA gravitational lensing and MUSE stellar dynamics

method.value: Simultaneously fit ALMA Band 7 lensing (via PyAutoLens with custom MGE deflection angles + elliptical NFW + external shear, scaled by (1 + eta_PPN)/2) and MUSE V_rms kinematics (via JAM with MGE stellar + MGE-parametrized NFW potential) across a 5-phase pipeline (Ph1: Sersic source; Ph2: Voronoi pixelization hyperparameters; Ph3: lens+JAM refinement I; Ph4: brightness-based Voronoi K-means hyperparameters; Ph5: lens+JAM refinement II with 300-seed bootstrap likelihood cap), then compute Einstein radius and dark matter fraction.

evidence.quote: Unfortunately, `PyAutoLens` does not provide the MGE parametrization as an alternative to light or mass profile. For this reason, we implement the MGE deflection angle in the context of the `PyAutoLens` framework, whilst the light and dark matter mass parametrizations were performed using the `MgeFit` package (cite: Cappellari2002).

To solve the axisymmetric Jeans equations and compute the projected second velocity moment, we use the Jeans Anisotropic Modelling (cite: Cappellari2008; Cappellari2020), in its Python implementation.

Since the lensing and the kinematical data are independent, we can consider the individual likelihoods of each model separately, such that we can produce a single likelihood for the combined modelling by multiplying the respective likelihoods:

key_parameters.value: 10 free parameters in Ph5 (Upsilon_0, delta, upsilon_0, kappa_s, q_DM, i, beta_z, shear_mag, shear_phi, eta_PPN); fixed NFW scale radius r_s = 10 * R_eff = 11.4''; 300 K-means seed evaluations for Ph5 lens likelihood cap

evidence.quote: Using the MP$_3$ and MP$_4$ results, we compute 300 likelihood evaluations, each of them using a different K-means seed.

Since we do not have enough data to constrain the dark matter halo on larger scales, we fix $r_s$ as 10 times the effective radius ($R_{\text{eff}} =  1.14\ensuremath{''}$) of the stellar component (cite: Kravtsov2013; Sonnenfeld2015).

To summarise, our fiducial model during the Ph5 has ten free parameters: three related to the stellar mass component ($\Upsilon_0, \delta, \upsilon_0$); two related to the dark matter halo component ($\kappa_s, q_{\text{\tiny{DM}}}$); one inclination ($i$); one parameter describing the anisotropy ($\beta_z$); two describing the effects of a possible external shear in the lens model ($\text{shear}_{\text{mag}}, \text{shear}_{\phi}$); and the gravitational slip parameter ($\eta_{\text{PPN}}$).

assumptions.value: Planck 2015 LCDM cosmology (H_0 = 67.7 km s^-1 Mpc^-1, Omega_Lambda = 0.6911, Omega_m = 0.3089); dark matter halo centre and orientation aligned with stellar component; constant orbital anisotropy beta_z; no SMBH in fiducial model.

evidence.quote: Throughout the paper, unless otherwise stated, the cosmological parameters assumed are: $H_0 = 67.7$ km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$, $\Omega_{\Lambda} = 0.6911$, $\Omega_{m} = 0.3089$ (cite: Planck_2015).
We also assume that the dark matter centre, the luminous mass centre, and the lens light centre coincide.
Additionally, we do not include the contribution of a supermassive black hole (SMBH), since the spatial resolution of the IFU data would not allow imposing strong constrains on this parameter.

fitting.value: Static nested sampling with dynesty using multiple ellipsoids bounding, random walk proposal (N_walks = 15), 180 live points (100 in Ph2), dlogz = 10 in Ph1-Ph2 and dlogz = 0.8 in Ph3-Ph5; joint likelihood L_Model = L_Lens * L_Dyn; Ph1 prior on eta_PPN is N[1.00, 0.09].

evidence.quote: For all pipeline phases, we use the static version of `dynesty`. We employ a multiple ellipsoids bounding distribution (cite: Mukherjee_2006; Feroz_2019), which can better handle with multi-modal distributions, and a random walk proposal sampling (cite: Metropolis; Hastings1970) with $N_{\text{walks}} = 15$.

Since in the first two phases, we are only interested in estimating a marginal region of the parameter space where the model has physical solutions, we define the termination criteria (cite: Skilling2006) as `dlogz`$= 10$. On the other hand, in the last three phases, the termination criteria are `dlogz`$= 0.8$. Moreover, as the multi-dimensional parameter space has many dimensions, we use a total of 180 live points in each phase, except for Ph2, which runs with 100 live points.

validation.value: Verified that MGE parametrization of elliptical NFW profile introduces only ~0.04% error in the deflection angle.

evidence.quote: We conclude that the error related to this parametrization in the deflection angle is of the order of $0.04\%$.

analysis_steps.goal: Quantify systematic uncertainties from mass profile, cosmology, and stellar kinematics

method.value: Re-run the 5-phase pipeline for 3 alternative mass models (r_s = 5 R_eff, free r_s, and Wong et al. 2015 composite model with spherical NFW + constant M/L + SMBH) and 5 alternative H_0 values (67.28, 68.20, 74.2, 72.2, 76.2 km s^-1 Mpc^-1), combine with the kinematic template dispersion difference (XSL vs MILES), and add systematic uncertainties in quadrature.

evidence.quote: First, we fix the dark matter radius to be 5 times the effective radius, for which we infer a $\eta_{\text{PPN}} = 1.12^{+0.03}_{-0.02}$ , and a fraction of dark matter within the Einstein ring consistent with $f_{\text{DM}} \sim 35\%$. Next, although our data do not cover the possible extended halo of dark matter, we consider the dark matter scale radius as a free parameter.

We now can combine in quadrature all the systematic uncertainties to estimate our final inference on the slip parameter: $0.017$ due to the effects related to the mass model adopted, $0.043$ related to the uncertainty on the cosmology, and $0.19$ uncertainty from the kinematic fit.

key_parameters.value: Alternative mass models: r_s = 5 R_eff, r_s free, Wong2015-like; alternative H_0 = 67.28, 68.20, 72.2, 74.2, 76.2 km s^-1 Mpc^-1; stellar libraries: MILES and XSL DR2

evidence.quote: Therefore, we opt to run the fiducial model again, however with different values of the Hubble constant, defined by the lower ($H_0 = 67.28$ km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$) and upper ($H_0 = 68.20$ km s$^{-1}$ Mpc$^{-1}$) values of the $1\sigma$ confidence level.
re-deriving the kinematic map using the Medium resolution INT Library of Empirical Spectra (cite: Miles_models) and the X-Shooter Spectral Library (cite: XSL).

assumptions.value: Systematic uncertainties from mass model, cosmology, and kinematics are independent and can be summed in quadrature.

evidence.quote: We now can combine in quadrature all the systematic uncertainties to estimate our final inference on the slip parameter: $0.017$ due to the effects related to the mass model adopted, $0.043$ related to the uncertainty on the cosmology, and $0.19$ uncertainty from the kinematic fit.

fitting.value: Standard deviation across alternative mass models (0.017) and across 6 H_0 runs (0.043), plus propagation of mean 3.4% velocity dispersion template offset into 13.6% (0.19) uncertainty on eta_PPN.

evidence.quote: Taking the standard deviation between the different values of $\eta_{\text{PPN}}$ for these alternative mass models, we can estimate an additional systematic uncertainty of the order of $0.017$ on the slip parameter.

Considering the standard deviation of the values of $\eta_{\text{PPN}}$ inferred for this six values of $H_0$, we infer an additional uncertainty of the order of $0.043$ on the slip parameter, related to the uncertainty on the Hubble constant.

Assuming the mean of these values, we expect a systematic of the order of $3.4\%$ due to poor kinematic constraints. This $3.4\%$ uncertainty on the velocity dispersion is responsible for a $13.6\%$ uncertainty on $\eta_{\text{PPN}}$.

claims.hypothesis: General Relativity with a vanishing anisotropic stress tensor predicts the gravitational slip parameter eta_PPN = 1 on galactic scales at intermediate redshift (z = 0.299).
claims.experiment: Simultaneously modelled ALMA Band 7 gravitational lensing and VLT/MUSE spatially-resolved stellar kinematics of the SDP.81 lens galaxy using a self-consistent MGE stellar + elliptical NFW dark matter mass profile, and quantified systematics from alternative mass profiles, Hubble constant values, and stellar spectral libraries.
claims.finding: The inferred gravitational slip parameter is consistent with General Relativity within 1 sigma once systematic uncertainties are included.

evidence.quote: We infer, after accounting for systematic uncertainties related to the mass model, cosmology and kinematics, $\eta_{\text{PPN}} = 1.13^{+0.03}_{-0.03}\pm0.20\,(\text{sys})$, which is in accordance with GR predictions.
We then infer that the most probable value for the slip parameter is $\eta_{\text{PPN}} = 1.13^{+0.03}_{-0.03}\pm0.20\,(\text{sys})$, which recovers GR within $1\sigma$ level.

claims.hypothesis: The dominant source of uncertainty in galaxy-scale tests of eta_PPN at intermediate redshift is systematic error from stellar kinematic measurements rather than mass profile parameterization or Hubble constant tension.
claims.experiment: Evaluated systematic shifts in eta_PPN across 3 alternative mass models, 5 alternative H_0 values (spanning Planck and late-Universe time-delay values), and 2 alternative stellar template libraries (MILES and XSL).
claims.result: Systematic uncertainties on eta_PPN are 0.017 from the mass model, 0.043 from cosmology (H_0), and 0.19 (13.6%) from the stellar kinematics (3.4% mean velocity dispersion offset).
claims.finding: Stellar kinematics, limited by spectral SNR at the galaxy outskirts and stellar template choice, is the dominant source of systematic uncertainty.

evidence.quote: We now can combine in quadrature all the systematic uncertainties to estimate our final inference on the slip parameter: $0.017$ due to the effects related to the mass model adopted, $0.043$ related to the uncertainty on the cosmology, and $0.19$ uncertainty from the kinematic fit.

The uncertainty introduced by our lack of knowledge about the kinematic properties is of the order of $0.19$, and ally with the low SNR at the outskirts of the lens galaxy is the main source of systematics in our analysis.

why_this_data.value: ALMA Band 7 provides tens-of-parsec resolution of the lensed submm source without contamination from the foreground lens galaxy light, while HST F160W traces the lens stellar mass distribution and VLT/MUSE provides spatially-resolved stellar kinematics.

evidence.quote: To impose constraints on $\eta_{\text{PPN}}$, combining different datasets that provide complementary information about the same massive object is necessary. The dataset used in this work is composed of high-resolution photometric data from the Hubble Space Telescope (HST), IFS data from the Multi-Unit Spectroscopic Explorer (MUSE), and interferometric data from ALMA.

Due to the wavelength observed by ALMA, the lens light is not visible, and only the deflected source is captured, making this dataset very suitable for lens modelling since the contamination due to the lens galaxy light is negligible.

why_this_method.value: Image-plane lens modelling allows masking background sky and fitting thousands of pixels instead of millions of visibilities for computational efficiency; MGE parametrization provides an analytical deprojection and simple Gaussian quadrature for both the lensing deflection angle and axisymmetric JAM kinematics; the 5-phase pipeline with a parametric Phase 1 and Phase 5 likelihood cap avoids unphysical under/over-magnified SLI solutions and Voronoi discretization spikes.

evidence.quote: Furthermore, the intrinsic stellar luminosity density (i.e. the deprojected quantity) has an analytical form for this parametrization. At the same time, the gravitational potential can be evaluated using a single and simple Gaussian quadrature.

In this work, we opt to perform the modelling in the image plane instead of the visibility plane of ALMA data since it allows us to mask and fit only the regions where the emission of the lensed source is detected. Furthermore, this choice makes the modelling more computationally efficient (we model thousands of pixels instead of millions of visibilities)
To avoid the under/over-magnified solutions, we initialize the modelling considering a parametric source profile, for which these unphysical solutions do not exist.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Using the lens-subtracted HST image for lens modelling was rejected because better ALMA interferometric data were available.

evidence.quote: After modelling the lens galaxy light profile and subtracting it from the original image, the deflected source is revealed. However, the lens-subtracted image is not used for modelling since better interferometric data are available.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Assigning an independent free M/L parameter to each MGE Gaussian component was rejected in favour of a 3-parameter Gaussian-modulated M/L profile to avoid introducing too many free parameters.

evidence.quote: Instead of using a different $M/L$ for each MGE component, which can introduce a lot of free parameters in our model, we opt to use a $M/L$ modulated by a Gaussian function

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Visibility-plane lens modelling of the ALMA data was rejected in favour of image-plane modelling for computational efficiency and spatial masking.

evidence.quote: In this work, we opt to perform the modelling in the image plane instead of the visibility plane of ALMA data since it allows us to mask and fit only the regions where the emission of the lensed source is detected.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Deriving angular diameter distances model-independently from Type Ia supernovae (Pan-STARRS1) was rejected because SN Ia samples only reach z < 2.3, below the source redshift z_s = 3.042.

evidence.quote: However, it is necessary to have supernovae data covering the redshift range of both lens and source galaxies, which is currently limited by $z < 2.3$, considering the Pan-STARRS1 Medium Deep Survey sample (cite: Scolnic_2018), which is far below the redshift of our source galaxy ($z_s = 3.042$).

how_they_decided_enough.value: Used dynesty stopping criteria dlogz = 10 in Ph1-Ph2 to locate the physical parameter space and dlogz = 0.8 in Ph3-Ph5 with 180 live points (100 in Ph2) and 300 K-means seed evaluations for the Ph5 likelihood cap.

evidence.quote: Using the MP$_3$ and MP$_4$ results, we compute 300 likelihood evaluations, each of them using a different K-means seed.

Since in the first two phases, we are only interested in estimating a marginal region of the parameter space where the model has physical solutions, we define the termination criteria (cite: Skilling2006) as `dlogz`$= 10$. On the other hand, in the last three phases, the termination criteria are `dlogz`$= 0.8$.

limitations_admitted.value: Cleaning visibilities into an image correlates pixels by the synthesized beam, which can bias image-plane modelling if pixel covariance is not accounted for.

evidence.quote: As a consequence of the procedure of obtaining an image from the visibilities, the image pixels become correlated by the beam, which could bias the image-plane modelling if the uncertainties do not take into account the covariance between the pixels.

limitations_admitted.value: MUSE spectroscopic data have low SNR in the galaxy outskirts, preventing strong constraints on the orbital anisotropy beta_z, the dark matter halo scale radius r_s, or a central SMBH.

evidence.quote: Since we do not have enough data to constrain the dark matter halo on larger scales, we fix $r_s$ as 10 times the effective radius ($R_{\text{eff}} =  1.14\ensuremath{''}$) of the stellar component (cite: Kravtsov2013; Sonnenfeld2015).
Additionally, we do not include the contribution of a supermassive black hole (SMBH), since the spatial resolution of the IFU data would not allow imposing strong constrains on this parameter.
Nevertheless, as evidenced by the anisotropy posterior distribution, this parameter is not well constrained by the kinematical data.

limitations_admitted.value: Assuming a LCDM cosmology to compute angular diameter distances introduces a circularity when testing General Relativity.

evidence.quote: Although, assuming a cosmology derived under the $\Lambda$CDM can raise discussions about the recursion of testing GR using predictions of itself.

referee_caveats_inferred: Priors in Phases 3 and 5 are iteratively narrowed around the previous phase median (MP_1 +- 20% or 1 sigma in Ph3; MP_3 +- 10% or 1 sigma in Ph5), and a informative Gaussian prior N(1.00, 0.09) is placed on eta_PPN in Phase 1, which can artificially shrink statistical posteriors.
Image-plane lens modelling of cleaned ALMA maps neglects off-diagonal pixel-to-pixel noise covariance introduced by the synthesized beam.
Text in Section 4.5 says the MGE fit was performed on the HST/F160W image, whereas the Table 1 caption labels the MGE components as coming from the HST/F110W image.
